solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reluctant to admit City's using primitive computer system?

indicators.note: to admit something is to let it in, so one word takes the other inside

parts.note: loth is an old spelling of loath, meaning unwilling
EC is the postcode for the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that a city is unwilling to own up to running on ancient computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-technology describes equipment that is basic and unsophisticated, as a primitive computer setup would be.

clue.text: Phone a posh female up for assistance

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the whole string is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to phone is to dial a number
gel is how an upper-class speaker supposedly says girl

explanation.surface: An instruction to ring a well-bred woman for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DIALAGEL around in this down entry. Legal aid is the UK state scheme paying lawyers for those who cannot afford them.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal aid is a form of public help with the cost of lawyers, so it is a kind of assistance.

clue.text: Court case involving British and French individual

indicators.note: involving means wrapping round, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: a case heard in court is a trial
un is French for one

explanation.surface: A legal case in which a Briton and a Frenchman are both caught up.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribunal is a body that sits in judgment, a kind of court.

clue.text: Officer left unloaded gun

parts.note: CO stands for commanding officer

indicators.note: with its contents emptied out, the word keeps only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An officer abandons a gun after taking out its bullets.
explanation.definitionFit: The Colt is a famous make of revolver, named after Samuel Colt.

clue.text: Like people with money, no doubt idle, casually circulating

indicators.note: circulating means going round, so the jumbled letters surround the inserted word
done casually, the letters of idle are thrown together in a loose new order

parts.note: no doubt means certain, sure

explanation.surface: The wealthy are idle, without question, as they wander casually about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casually' makes LEID, which 'circulating' wraps around the 'no doubt' word; 'idle' looks like part of the definition but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The leisured classes have free time because they have wealth, so they are like people with money.

clue.text: Gets rid of old time dancing in east

parts.note: ex as a prefix means former or old
a term is a period of time

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle into a new order

explanation.surface: Old-time dancing is being banished from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' turns IN EAST into INATES. 'old time dancing' looks like one phrase, but splits into three jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To exterminate is to destroy completely, a forceful way of getting rid of something.

clue.text: Ace Matisse redraft showing animal

indicators.note: to redraft is to rewrite, here the letters are rewritten in another order

explanation.surface: An expert redrawing of a Matisse picture shows a creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of domestic cat, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Service offered by two engineers?

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a pair is a set of two

explanation.surface: A job done by a couple of engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a car serviced means it is checked and mended, which is repair work.

clue.text: I deride short, funny-looking Frenchman

indicators.note: funny-looking suggests something oddly shaped, so these letters are rearranged
short means cut off at the end, losing the final letter

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to mocking a small, odd-looking man from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts DERIDE to DERID, and 'funny-looking' rearranges I and DERID.
explanation.definitionFit: Didier is a common French given name, so it can stand for a Frenchman.

clue.text: Questions Greece's problems

parts.note: GR is the international code for Greece
ills are troubles or problems

explanation.surface: Someone raises doubts about Greece's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill someone is to interrogate them hard, firing questions at them.

clue.text: Punished, having little money

definitions.meaning: beaten with a leather belt, as a punishment
the informal sense of short of cash

explanation.surface: Someone is both disciplined and broke.
explanation.definitionFit: Strapped means beaten with a strap, and 'strapped for cash' means hard up.

clue.text: Admits over six pounds will keep occupant of property slightly short

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one word sits within the other

parts.note: C is the Roman hundred, and a hundred ounces is a little more than six pounds

indicators.note: slightly short means the word loses just its final letter

parts.note: a tenant occupies a rented property

explanation.surface: Someone confesses that a heavy weight will hold a slightly undersized resident.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly short' trims the last letter; 'will keep' holds the result. C is a Roman hundred, and a hundred ounces is just over six pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To countenance something is to tolerate or allow it, as when one admits a practice.

clue.text: Uncouth person, the last to travel abroad

indicators.note: the last of the word means its final letter only

parts.note: abroad means out and about, outside

explanation.surface: A boor is the final one to go overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: A lout is a rough, ill-mannered man, an uncouth person.

clue.text: Middle-class compulsion to get round in city of Idaho

indicators.note: in places the joined letters inside the city's name

parts.note: Boise is the state capital of Idaho
an urge is a compelling desire
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A conventional urge to travel around an Idaho city.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourgeois, feminine bourgeoise, describes the conventional, property-owning middle class.

clue.text: Drowned by Rolling Stones, female with piano accompaniment offers Rocket Man?

indicators.note: drowned by means submerged in, so the other letters sit inside the word
rolling stones tumble, so their letters tumble into a new order

parts.note: P is the musical marking for piano, softly
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A woman singing at a piano is drowned out by the Rolling Stones, then presents a song about a rocket man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling' makes STESON, and 'Drowned by' puts PHEN inside it. Elton John's song 'Rocket Man' is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: George Stephenson built the Rocket locomotive, so he is a Rocket man, punning on the Elton John song.

clue.text: Given temporary shelter, say, setter's distracted

indicators.note: say signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: someone given temporary shelter is in a tent
the setter says I have, contracted to I've

explanation.surface: The setter, having been put up somewhere briefly, is absent-minded.
explanation.definitionFit: Inattentive means not paying attention, so a distracted person is this.

clue.text: PM is protected by doctor and a priest

indicators.note: something protected by another is enclosed by it, so it sits inside

parts.note: Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A prime minister is guarded by a doctor and a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Disraeli was twice British Prime Minister in the 19th century.

clue.text: Plant that's quite sizeable in Knutsford's borders?

indicators.note: in sets the phrase between the edges of the town's name
the borders of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: quite sizeable is not wee, wee being Scottish for small

explanation.surface: A rather large plant is growing at the edges of Knutsford, a Cheshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Knotweed is a plant, the Japanese kind being a notorious invasive weed.

clue.text: Rehearsal in theatre, with assistant helping all round

indicators.note: all round means the two words together surround the other piece

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant
rep is repertory theatre
a helping or portion is a ration

explanation.surface: A rehearsal in a theatre, with an assistant lending a hand all over.
explanation.definitionFit: Preparation is the work of getting ready, and a rehearsal readies a cast for performance.

clue.text: Rule with symbol of authority over a part of Africa

parts.note: a wand or rod of office symbolises power

explanation.surface: Someone governs with a staff of office over a region of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Rwanda is a country in east-central Africa.

clue.text: Musical instrument is my bag

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like 'my!'
a net is a mesh bag

explanation.surface: Someone claims a musical instrument as their own luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' reads as a possessive but is the exclamation 'My!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cornet is a brass instrument like a small trumpet.

clue.text: Stockist has problem acquiring salt, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the words are judged by their sound

parts.note: a hole is a problem, and a salt is an old sailor, so this is a hole getting a sailor

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper has trouble getting hold of salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler holds stock in bulk to sell on to shops, so is a kind of stockist.

clue.text: Worry there's some bitter feuding during revolution

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the letters are read backwards
some means only part of the phrase is used, a run of its letters

explanation.surface: Anxiety over the bitter feuds that break out in a revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes TERF from the end of 'bitter' and start of 'feuding'; 'during revolution' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and agitated, to worry.

clue.text: Plant falls over when regularly neglected

indicators.note: neglecting letters at regular intervals leaves every other one, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A plant topples when it is not watered often enough.
explanation.definitionFit: The aloe is a succulent plant, known for the soothing aloe vera.

clue.text: Unique individual providing service at London hospital

parts.note: nones is the church service of the ninth hour
UCH is University College Hospital in London

explanation.surface: A singular person who holds a service at a London hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonesuch is a person or thing without equal, a paragon.

clue.text: Do run away from church

parts.note: to run away is to flee
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An order to escape from the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To do someone is slang for cheating them, the same as to fleece them.

clue.text: Surprise when on this, getting high

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: getting high suggests letters intoxicated and lurching into another order

explanation.surface: A shock when someone on drugs gets high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting high' rearranges ON THIS into TONISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish is to amaze, to take by surprise.

clue.text: Responsible for live animal

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
a hind is a female deer

explanation.surface: Someone is in charge of a living creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Being behind something means being the cause of it, as in 'who was behind the plot?'
